source.title: Stochastic Function Norm Regularization of Deep Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material. Its title differs slightly from the provided title; the text is coherent and appears complete.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares dropout with a different regularizer on held-out classification performance, but does not test the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior work on random-label fitting, batch size and sharp minima; those cited results are not rows. Figure-only values are not read from the plots.
record.test_reason: The MNIST experiments include dropout versus no-dropout controls and dropout added to function-norm regularization in a small-data setting, bearing on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' qualitative MNIST conclusion, including the tentative benefit of combining dropout with function-norm regularization. Their broader conclusion also covers function-norm computational hardness, a generalization bound, and empirical improvements on Oxford Flowers and Cityscapes.
record.recipe_differences: Adds weighted function norm regularization and compares it with dropout; the MNIST models use plain SGD with momentum.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization batch size changes the reported performance and variance; batch normalization appears to eliminate the L2 norm effect. Two Gaussian sampling settings diverged and yielded random performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Weighted function-norm regularization outperforms competing regularizers on classification and improves ENet validation performance on Cityscapes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling-based function-norm regularization can improve held-out performance in low-data settings.

record.code_released: Source code will be released at the time of publication.
record.problems: The dropout comparisons are mainly presented as plots; numerical values are not stated. Results use small MNIST training subsets and do not isolate dropout's effect against the no-regularization condition in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported in text or tables. Other numerical performance traces appear only in figures and do not separately measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in matched architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Training-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Larger training sets, dropout-rate dependence and excessive-dropout underfitting; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparative ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: A matched comparison of function-norm regularization with versus without added dropout. The text reports tentative additional improvement; neither existing row records this comparison.

Supplementary MNIST comparisons with versus without dropout using 300 training examples and otherwise identical architecture and optimization hyperparameters. Figure 8 contains these conditions, although the supplied text does not establish their individual dropout effects numerically.
missing.locator: Supplementary Section E.2; Figure 8a–b and caption

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text preserves plot legends and axes but does not reliably expose individual curve values. Superiority of the proposed regularizer over dropout alone does not establish whether dropout improves over its matched no-dropout control. Regularization-sample batch sizes do not test V5.

versions.untested_parts: The reported comparison does not give recoverable numerical dropout effects versus no regularization, or test small training sets generally or dropout rates.
